producer_report.summary: A drain attempt that ends as "needs accepting" now gives its job slot back, so a batch with `--job-limit` 1 goes on to the next item. The cause was in `run_job` in `crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs`. It took a slot (`st.started += 1`) before the read and never released it. Every re-read that came back needing acceptance therefore used up a slot, and the next item hit the job limit. The `_ if run.needs_accepting` arm of `run_job` now does `st.started = st.started.saturating_sub(1)` under the state lock. The cost of the attempt stays in the budget. The JobLimit check and the passed, held, failed and budget outcomes are unchanged. I updated the drain module docs, the `Limits::max_jobs` doc, the `--job-limit` doc and the stop-reasons help in `main.rs` to say such a re-read does not count. I added a Fixed entry to CHANGELOG.md. The new test is `a_needs_accepting_reread_does_not_use_a_job_slot`. I ran the whole drain test file, fmt, the policy scan and clippy for athena-cli; the full workspace `cargo test` is left to Athena.

checks_run.note: 162 tests passed, including the new one, the_job_limit_stops_the_loop, an_urgent_queued_request_is_worked_before_an_approved_in_limit_proposal, both existing needs-accepting tests, and drain_help_documents_the_flags_and_lists_every_stop_reason.

checks_run.command: cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain a_needs_accepting_reread_does_not_use_a_job_slot (with the decrement temporarily changed to saturating_sub(0))
checks_run.note: Expected failure without the fix. The log was ["run a"] instead of ["run a","run b","land b"]: b never started because of the job limit. I then restored the decrement and the test passes.
Run for athena-cli only, not the whole workspace.
17 tests passed, including the boundary scan.

criteria_check.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs (Grep for `needs_accepting` near `max_jobs: 1`) drains with job limit 1 where item `a` ends as needs accepting and item `b` is runnable. It asserts `jobs[0].outcome == "needs accepting"`, `landed == 1`, and `stop != Stop::JobLimit`. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain` and it passes.
criteria_check.evidence: `a_needs_accepting_reread_does_not_use_a_job_slot` is in tests/drain.rs. It uses Stub with needs_accepting ["a"] and Limits max_jobs 1, and asserts jobs[0].outcome == "needs accepting", landed == 1 and stop != Stop::JobLimit. I ran `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`: 162 passed, 0 failed.

criteria_check.criterion: The same test, run against the unfixed `run_job` counter (as in the pre-change source in `git diff`), would stop with `Stop::JobLimit` before `b` runs. The assertions show it fails without the fix: `b` is asserted to land, which the old counter prevents.
criteria_check.evidence: I changed the decrement to saturating_sub(0), which is the old behaviour, and ran the new test. It failed: log ["run a"] against the expected ["run a","run b","land b"]. I restored the fix and the test passes.

criteria_check.criterion: `git diff` of crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs shows the `RunStep::NeedsAccepting` path in `run_job` giving the started-job slot back (a decrement of `st.started` under the state lock). The JobLimit check and the other outcomes (Failed, Held, Passed) are unchanged.
criteria_check.evidence: The diff adds a block in the `_ if run.needs_accepting` arm: `let mut st = self.st(); st.started = st.started.saturating_sub(1);`. The `st.started >= self.limits.max_jobs` check and the other arms are untouched. The rest of the diff is doc comments.

criteria_check.criterion: A job limit that still binds for ordinary jobs: `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain` still passes `the_job_limit_stops_the_loop`, `an_urgent_queued_request_is_worked_before_an_approved_in_limit_proposal`, and the two existing needs-accepting tests, with no existing assertions weakened (`git diff` shows no removed asserts in them).
criteria_check.evidence: All four tests passed in the 162-test run of `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain`. The change to tests/drain.rs only adds a new test function and removes no lines.

criteria_check.criterion: `cargo test` passes for the workspace and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.
criteria_check.evidence: left to Athena's checks. I ran `cargo fmt --all --check` (clean), `cargo clippy -p athena-cli --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` (clean), the full athena-cli drain test file (pass) and `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` (pass). criteria_check.criterion: Doc comments or help text in crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs that describe the job limit (the `--job-limit` help and the module docs near ~line 180) say a re-read that only needs accepting does not count toward it. A Grep for that wording finds it.
criteria_check.evidence: Added the wording "does not count toward `--job-limit`" to the drain.rs module docs (configuration-change bullet) and the `Limits::max_jobs` doc. Added "does not count" to the main.rs `--job-limit` doc comment and the "job limit" stop-reasons help line. The drain help test still passes.

mistakes: My first attempt to run the drain tests piped the output through `tail`, which the hook refused. I reran without the pipe.
learnings: `Stub::run` in tests/drain.rs logs `run <job>`, and `Stub::read` logs `read <job>`, so log assertions on the Stub need a filter or the `read` entries included.

In `run_job` the slot is taken before the read and the only place that sees a needs-accepting outcome is after `steps.run`. The release therefore belongs in that arm, with the slot held during the read and run so parallel workers cannot overshoot the limit.
The Bash tool here allows only cargo, git, ls and similar; piping to tail is blocked.
